item.title: No. 3 Florida Basketball Survives to Avoid Huge Upset
item.description: Photo by: Alan Youngblood The No. 3 Florida Gators narrowly avoided one of the biggest upsets of the college basketball season Tuesday night, defeating Milwaukee 76-67 at Tower Hill Arena in Gainesville. Florida entered the matchup as a massive favorite, expected to handle a Milwaukee team that had struggled through the early portion of its season. Instead, the Gators found themselves in a much closer contest than anticipated, needing a strong second-half performance to secure the nine-point victory. The win improves Florida’s record to 7-1, but the performance raises questions about a team that entered the season with national championship expectations. Milwaukee Gives Florida a Scare Milwaukee deserves credit for making this a competitive game. The Panthers played with confidence and refused to back down against one of the nation’s top teams. Florida was favored by more than 30 points, but Milwaukee managed to keep the game within reach throughout the first half. The Panthers trailed just 37-34 at halftime, putting pressure on the Gators to find another gear after the break. The game remained competitive deep into the second half, with Milwaukee cutting Florida’s lead to just two points at one stage. For a team expected to cruise to an easy victory, the Gators suddenly found themselves in danger of suffering an embarrassing home loss. Milwaukee’s Chandler Jackson led the Panthers with 20 points, while Al Amadou contributed 13. The Panthers also knocked down 10 three pointers, making it difficult for Florida to create separation. Rueben Chinyelu Comes Up Huge The biggest reason Florida escaped with the victory was the outstanding performance from Rueben Chinyelu. Chinyelu delivered a career high 25 points and grabbed 16 rebounds, recording his first double-double of the season. He was extremely efficient, shooting 10-of-12 from the field and making all four of his free throws. When Florida needed someone to take control, Chinyelu answered. His presence around the basket helped the Gators establish an advantage inside, and his offensive rebounding gave Florida important second-chance opportunities. Thomas Haugh also delivered a strong performance, finishing with 16 points and eight rebounds. Denzel Aberdeen added 14 points, providing another important scoring option. Florida ultimately controlled the paint, outscoring Milwaukee 40-22 in that area while winning the rebounding battle 45-24. Gators Have Plenty to Clean Up Although Florida avoided the upset, Tuesday’s performance showed that the team still has plenty of work to do. The Gators cannot afford to overlook opponents, especially with a challenging schedule ahead. Their defensive intensity was inconsistent, allowing Milwaukee to remain within striking distance for much of the night. Head coach Todd Golden will likely use this performance as a teaching opportunity. item.title: Scoring Milestone | FC’s Hadli Gillum scores her 1,000th career point
item.description: LANCASTER - On a night when Fisher Catholic junior Hadli Gillum had a chance to reach a major scoring milestone, it wasn't a matter of if, but a matter of when she would do it. Needing 23 points to reach 1,000 career points, Gillum missed her first two shots, including an uncontested layup. Maybe it was nerves, maybe it was all the people in the stands, holding up signs and counting down, but for Gillum, she is a scorer, and it didn’t take her long to get going after those first two misses. Gillum scored 17 points in the first quarter against Cristo Rey, and after scoring two more baskets to get to 21 points, Gillum was to reach the 1,000-point plateau when she received the ball in the post, to a couple dribbles to her left, then quickly came back to the right and laid it in off the glass. Her teammates congratulated her, and the game stopped to recognize her accomplishment. More: Fisher Catholic's Hadli Gillum is a sophomore basketball sensation “This has definitely been a goal I’ve had my whole life, ever since I started watching my older sister play and past players like Voni Bethel. Watching them get it, it was a goal of mine coming into high school,” Gillum said. “I didn’t expect it to be this early, but I am very excited and grateful for the opportunity and the community and the support we have here. It was loud in here, and the love and support meant a lot to me. "It has been stressful only because everyone was talking about it, and my friends were asking what if I didn’t get it. I knew it was going to come eventually, so I wasn’t worried about it that much, although I did miss that easy layup early in the game, and all I could do was laugh.” Gillum, who only played in the first half as the Irish cruised to a 57-8 victory, scored 25 points on 12 of 18 shooting. She added four assists, three rebounds and four steals. Gillum has now scored 1,002 career points in 53 games played. Who knows where her career total will end up with basically two full seasons remaining. Gillum, who was the 2025 Eagle-Gazette Girls Basketball Player of the Year and earned first-team All-Ohio honors in both her freshman and sophomore seasons, has shown she can score in a variety of different ways. She is an outstanding passer, making sure she always gets her teammates involved. item.title: Georgia ranked No. 1 in fourth College Football Playoff rankings
item.description: The fourth edition of the 2026-27 College Football Playoff rankings was released on Nov. 24, and the Georgia Bulldogs stayed put as the top spot in the rankings for the third straight week in a row. They probably added some distance after blowing out South Carolina 34-6. They've beaten four straight ranked SEC opponents by double digits. They beat No. 17 (AP) Florida, No. 10 Ole Miss , No. 22 Missouri, and No. 21 South Carolina. With the win, they clinched a spot in the SEC championship, their sixth appearance in a row in the SEC championship. Considering the status of the SEC and the rest of the College Football Playoff, the Bulldogs are almost certain to make the CFP. Speaking of the SEC, the biggest surprises came with the way they dealt with the other three that are in the CFP: Texas, Tennessee, and Alabama. They rose Texas to the No. 3 spot, increased Tennessee to No. 5, and brought down Alabama to No. 6. The Big Ten also experienced a ton of changes. UCLA is the only team in the conference that's still in the CFP. They lost 18-16 in 3OT to Michigan, bringing them down from No. 4 to No. 9. Indiana, meanwhile, fell all the way down from No. 8 to No. 14 after their 27-24 overtime loss to Washington. The Oregon Ducks passed them up, becoming the No. 12 team and the first one out of the CFP. The Indiana fall brought in a new addition to the CFP: 10-1 Texas Tech. Once again, just like the last two weeks, Georgia would get a first-round bye if this holds. They would play the winner of the game between Wake Forest and UCLA. Both of those teams have a 10-1 record, but with very different resumes. Wake Forest has won by 21 or more points in their past seven games, while UCLA hasn't won by more than 20 against a Big Ten opponent since the Maryland game. It'll be a big test for either squad against Georgia. item.title: CFP chair Hunter Yurachek explains UCLA's No. 9 ranking
item.description: UCLA Bruins RB Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a rushing touchdown during a game against San Diego State Aztecs at Rose Bowl Stadium on September 12, 2026 in Pasadena, California. UCLA football dropped from No. 4 to No. 9 in the Nov. 24 edition of the College Football Playoff (CFP) rankings, marking one of the more notable shifts in this week’s top 25. The drop came after the Bruins’ first loss of the season, an 18-16 triple overtime contest at Michigan which put them at 10-1. Despite the loss, they remain the highest-ranked team in the Big Ten and the only Big Ten team currently in the playoff bracket, followed by No. 12 Oregon, who is currently the first team out. Other Big Ten teams still seemingly in contention include No. 13 Iowa and No. 14 Indiana, although the committee appears to believe UCLA currently has a somewhat sizable advantage over them. “UCLA right now is not evaluated with those other three teams,” CFP chair Hunter Yurachek told ESPN’s Rece Davis. “They do have the head-to-head over Oregon.” In a selection committee media teleconference following the release of the rankings, Yurachek noted that during this week’s discussions, the committee most directly compared UCLA to three teams not in their conference: No. 8 Wake Forest, No. 10 BYU and No. 11 Texas Tech. “Wake Forest is a hot team,” Yurachek said. “They’ve won eight consecutive games, and most of those games have not even been close. And so they’ve got a lot of respect for the committee. “UCLA also has a great deal of respect from the committee. We had them at four last week. They lost a triple overtime game on the road at Michigan, a team that was 5-5. They’ve got a win over a team that we currently have ranked 12th in Oregon, and then when you start comparing them to BYU, BYU’s a two-loss team. BYU’s got really good wins, one over Notre Dame and another over Arizona. They’ve got two losses, one to No. 2 Utah and then another to Central Florida, and so we start mixing and matching these teams, you look at strength of schedule, key wins, losses. That’s how that shook out with Wake Forest, UCLA, BYU, and Texas Tech.” Yurachek was adamant in multiple comments that the uncertain status of Bruins quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who was injured late in the game against Michigan, did not play a factor in where UCLA was ranked. “UCLA fell from four to nine because they lost the game in triple overtime to Michigan,” Yuracheck told Davis. “It did not have anything to do with the injury to the quarterback that happened in the overtime period.” “They played a game [for] four-plus quarters with him at quarterback,” he continued in the teleconference. “They had an overtime period that they did not have him. We’ll continue to evaluate UCLA in their game versus USC this weekend.”

item.description: Credit: ESPN Mark November 24, 2026 in the history books. It might be the first time the College Football Playoff committee seems to have quieted a majority of critics in its history. This year, like pretty much every year since it came into being, the CFP committee has been blasted for offering contradictory rankings that seemingly change on a whim on a weekly basis. And has been proven for years , the weekly ranking shows that air every Tuesday on ESPN are then thrown out the window and proven to be completely meaningless when the committee puts together the only rankings that actually matter at the end of the season. But that hasn’t stopped ESPN and the College Football Playoff committee for continuing the charade and raising the blood pressure of college football fans and media every week by continuing the drama. This year has been no exception, with the chief complaint being Alabama’s lofty ranking compared to, well, everyone else that watches college football. The Crimson Tide are still getting what seems to be a Nick Saban pass from the committee, being ranked consistently ahead of Tennessee even after a comprehensive head-to-head victory by the Volunteers. item.title: Vikings’ Kevin O’Connell Gets Blunt on Bijan Robinson Before Falcons Game
item.description: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings are looking for a bounce-back win after their Week 11 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Nonetheless, they’ll have a challenging task at home when they face the Atlanta Falcons, who are 3-7. Despite the Falcons’ record, they’ll be leaning on their weapons, one of them being running back Bijan Robinson. The Falcons star has played 460 total snaps this season, leading to an 84.6 overall PFF grade . Moreover, he carried the ball 185 times for 951 rushing yards and six touchdowns while averaging 5.1 yards per attempt on the ground and forcing 37 missed tackles as a runner. Meanwhile, as a receiver, he caught 35 passes on 42 targets for 256 receiving yards and one touchdown. As a result, Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell knows that they will need to contain Robinson if they want to secure a win. “I expect he’s going to get a high volume of carries,” O’Connell said on the Nov. 24 edition of “X’s and O’s with Kevin O’Connell.” “I expect they’ll try to come in here and run the football. We have to have a great day shutting down the run. We have to have a great day tackling, making sure there are no loose-yardage plays. “When Bijan breaks a tackle, it’s not like he’s just going to gain another three or four yards. He can take it the distance at any time [and] he can catch it. He’s a part of their passing game and lethal in the screen game. On top of all the things they present with Bijan, you have to know where he is and what they’re trying to do at all times to get him involved in the game.” KOC on Whether Falcons Will Look to Copy 49ers’ Game Plan Furthermore, O’Connell talked about whether he sees the Falcons looking to copy anything that the 49ers did against them to try and secure a road win over Minnesota. “I think the copycat nature of the league is more about the principles of things people do,” O’Connell added. “What was the intent? item.description: Stephen A. Smith raised some eyebrows last Wednesday when he called out the NBA for potentially letting the Lakers win a championship. A team that’s led by a trio of white stars in Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler. The talk show personality faced a lot of scrutiny and criticism for his comments. He questioned Black NBA players for letting a group of “white brothers” “win a championship.” Stephen A. Smith reveals Black NBA players have shared their support about his white player Lakers comments. ZUMAPRESS.com But even with the scrutiny, he’s also received support. The television personality revealed on his show, “Straight Shooter,” on Tuesday night that Black NBA players have reached out to him to thank him for his comments about the Lakers trio. “You know how many brothers in the NBA reached out to me and thanked me for saying it?” Smith said. When the Lakers trio was finished being assembled in July when Los Angeles acquired Kessler via a sign-and-trade deal with the Jazz, Smith questioned the team’s decision to form the trio and said, “Your three best players are white dudes. This ain’t golf. And we got a whole bunch of brothers on Team USA. This is basketball, what y’all think this is?” Stephen A. NBAE via Getty Images The Lakers entered Tuesday night tied for the NBA’s best record with the Spurs (15-3) and have been led by Dončić, who’s an early MVP candidate. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. United on Saturday. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
